Short answer: Canadians never wanted to be part of the USA. Two and half-centuries on, people still don´t want to.  It´s literally a country founded by people who did not want to be Americans.

Question about Americans invading Canada: In both 1770´s and 1812, they could have gone north along the Hudson to Lake Champlain, and then North from Lake Champlain on the Richelieu River, which is navigable all the way to the St-Lawrence (aside from a little portage.)  It´s not clear to me why the Americans chose to traverse hundreds of km. of wilderness instead.  They could have taken St-Jean sur Richelieu and made that their base for further invasions, with very good supply lines from the south.

This is the route a heck of a lot of empire loyalists took after the war, to the point of founding Sorel at the mouth of the Richelieu where it empties into the St-Laurent.  It seems really odd the Americans did not choose that route.

One detail on the war of 1812, which affected the American invasion was that the states on the Eastern seaboard refused to let their state militia to leave their state to invade. The bonds through commerce and family was very strong, and to invade “ Canada” was thought as attacking a friend. They were prepared to defend their state, but not attack. Thus militias from the south were used, who didn’t know the terrain and wasn’t used to it 
The USA had no national army then like it has now, only individual state militias. One of the after effects was that the USA would develop one, after great debate, because having a strong central government could lead to having a King, which they despise.
Good video, but while the borders remained the same,the biggest loser were the Ingenious people. Tecumseh, the main “leader” of a lot of First Nation tribes had been developing a plan for a united indigenous people so that they could oppose American expansion in the West before the war of 1812. He was a very charismatic leader, and put in with the British if the British would guarantee a land west of the Appellations. He got killed during the war, thus so did his dream.
If you are looking for topics about Canada, I would suggest that you maybe react to Canadian Heritage minutes. (YouTube has them all)
They are a minute long, and explore and highlight moments in Canadian history and culture. They may give you ideas for videos that can be looked at more in depth. 
I would recommend that you do a video on Terry Fox, and Tommy Douglas. Two people that made significant contributions to Canada!
